name: Daniel Wellington
tagline: The Instagram-era Scandinavian minimalist that redefined fashion-watch marketing
summary: Daniel Wellington is a Stockholm-based fashion watch brand founded in 2011 by Filip Tysander, famous for slim, minimalist quartz watches on interchangeable NATO, leather and mesh straps. Its pioneering influencer marketing turned it into one of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and in 2025 Timex Group acquired a 51% majority stake.
history:
Daniel Wellington was founded in Stockholm in 2011 by Swedish entrepreneur Filip Tysander. The brand's name and look came from a stylish British gentleman Tysander met while backpacking in Australia, who wore his vintage watches on faded NATO straps. Tysander launched with a small sum of savings, designing a clean, thin, eggshell-dial quartz watch with interchangeable straps, manufactured in China with Japanese Miyota movements.

Rather than traditional advertising, DW became one of the first consumer brands to scale almost entirely through Instagram, gifting watches to thousands of influencers and offering discount codes. The strategy was spectacularly successful: by 2016 the company reported roughly US$230 million in revenue with more than US$100 million in profit, and in 2017 it was named Europe's fastest-growing private company. Its Classic collection, with models named after British places such as Sheffield, Durham and St Mawes, became a defining accessory of the 2010s.

Growth stalled at the end of the decade as the fashion-watch category shrank, smartwatches surged and influencer marketing became crowded; DW posted several years of operating losses around 2019-2021. The brand responded by broadening into jewellery and new collections such as Iconic Link, Iconic Chronograph, GMT and automatic models. In 2022 Timex Group entered via a convertible loan and distribution partnership, and in November 2025 Timex acquired a 51% controlling stake. DW continues to operate from its Stockholm headquarters and remains one of the most recognisable fashion-watch names worldwide.

name: Michael Kors
tagline: Jet-set glamour on the wrist: the defining gold-tone fashion watch of the 2010s
summary: Michael Kors is the New York fashion label whose oversized, gold-tone chronographs and pavé-set ladies' watches became a global bestseller after Fossil Group began producing them under licence in 2004. The brand is owned by Capri Holdings, and Fossil's watch and jewellery licence has been extended through 2027.
history:
American designer Michael Kors (born Karl Anderson Jr.) launched his womenswear label in New York in 1981, selling to department stores such as Bergdorf Goodman. The business went through bankruptcy in 1993 before relaunching with lower-priced lines, while Kors also served as creative director of the French house Céline from 1997 to 2004 and later became a household name as a judge on Project Runway.

In April 2004 Michael Kors signed an exclusive watch licence with Fossil, the Texas-based fashion-watch giant. Fossil's design and distribution machine paired perfectly with Kors's jet-set aesthetic of oversized cases, gold-tone steel, chronograph sub-dials and crystal-set bezels. Collections such as Runway, Lexington, Parker and Darci became ubiquitous in department stores and airports worldwide, and by the early 2010s Michael Kors was one of the bestselling watch brands in markets such as the UK and US. Fossil added the fashion jewellery licence in 2010, and the pair renewed their agreement for ten years in 2014.

Michael Kors Holdings went public in 2011, bought Jimmy Choo in 2017 and Versace in 2018, and renamed itself Capri Holdings. As the fashion-watch category shrank in the late 2010s, Fossil also produced Michael Kors Access smartwatches. A proposed takeover of Capri by Tapestry was blocked in 2024, and in 2025 Capri sold Versace. In February 2025 Fossil and Michael Kors extended their licensing partnership through 2027, continuing a relationship of more than twenty years.

name: BOSS (Hugo Boss)
tagline: German tailoring house whose sharp chronographs are built by Movado Group
summary: Hugo Boss is the Metzingen-based fashion house behind the BOSS and HUGO labels. Its watches, mostly sporty quartz chronographs and dress pieces sold in department stores worldwide, have been designed, made and distributed under licence by Movado Group since 2005.
history:
Hugo Ferdinand Boss founded a clothing company in Metzingen, Germany, in 1924, initially producing workwear and uniforms. During the 1930s and 1940s the firm manufactured uniforms for the Nazi Party and German armed forces, using forced labour during the war, a history the company formally acknowledged and apologised for in 2011. After Boss's death in 1948 the business was run by his son-in-law Eugen Holy, whose sons Uwe and Jochen transformed it in the 1970s into an international menswear label known for sharp, power-dressing suits.

Hugo Boss went public in 1985 and was later controlled by the Italian Marzotto group and then private-equity firm Permira. The company expanded into womenswear, fragrance and accessories, much of it through licences. Watches arrived in the 1990s: from 1996 BOSS timepieces were produced by the licensee Tempus Concept, and in 2005 Movado Group took over a long-term global licence to design, manufacture and market BOSS and HUGO watches.

Under Movado, BOSS watches became a department-store staple, built around bold stainless-steel chronographs with motorsport and nautical themes such as Hero, Grand Prix, Santiago and Candor, alongside minimalist dress watches and a separate, younger HUGO line. In 2022 the partners renewed their licence through the end of 2026 and introduced BOSS watches made with recycled ocean-bound plastic. Today Hugo Boss AG remains listed in Frankfurt and headquartered in Metzingen.

name: Emporio Armani
tagline: Milanese minimalism for the wrist, made by Fossil since 1997
summary: Emporio Armani is the younger, more accessible line of Giorgio Armani's Milan fashion house. Its watches, designed and distributed by Fossil Group under licence since 1997, range from sleek quartz chronographs to open-heart automatics, solar World Explorers and a Swiss Made line.
history:
Giorgio Armani founded his fashion company in Milan in 1975 with his partner Sergio Galeotti, and in 1981 launched Emporio Armani, a younger, more affordable diffusion line identified by its eagle logo. The label became a pillar of the Armani empire, extending into denim, fragrance, eyewear and accessories through a network of licences.

Watches arrived in 1997, when the Armani Group signed Fossil to design, develop and distribute timepieces under the Emporio Armani name. The partnership grew steadily: jewellery was added in the early 2000s, Armani Exchange watches in 2008, and in 2014 the companies extended their global licence for ten years and launched Emporio Armani Swiss Made, a higher-priced collection produced in Switzerland. Emporio Armani watches became best-sellers in department stores and duty-free shops worldwide, known for clean dials, black-and-steel chronographs and, later, black ceramic cases.

In the smartwatch era Fossil produced Emporio Armani Connected touchscreen and hybrid smartwatches, while the core range shifted toward value mechanicals such as the open-heart Meccanico automatics and, more recently, solar-powered World Explorer and Sea Explorer models. Giorgio Armani led the company as sole shareholder and designer until his death in September 2025, after which ownership passed under the arrangements of his will and the Giorgio Armani Foundation. Emporio Armani watches continue to be made and sold by Fossil Group.

name: Gucci
tagline: The first fashion house to make watches, now crafting Swiss high horology
summary: Gucci, the Florentine luxury house owned by Kering, entered watchmaking in 1972 and was the first high-fashion label to do so. Its Swiss-made watches range from logo-rich quartz pieces like the G-Timeless and skate-inspired Grip to the 25H sports-luxe line and high-watchmaking tourbillons.
history:
Guccio Gucci founded his leather-goods house in Florence in 1921, and by the 1950s-60s Gucci had become a global symbol of Italian luxury. In 1972, under Aldo Gucci, the house struck a licensing deal with Severin Wunderman, whose Severin Montres began producing Gucci watches in Switzerland. Gucci is widely described as the first high-fashion house to expand into watchmaking.

The partnership was an immediate hit. The Gucci Model 2000 quartz watch reportedly sold more than a million units in two years, earning a Guinness World Record in the mid-1970s. Through the 1980s and 1990s Gucci watches, including bangle watches and interchangeable-bezel designs, became department-store and duty-free staples. In 1997 Gucci bought Severin Montres outright, bringing watch design and production in-house in Switzerland. Soon afterwards Gucci itself came under the control of PPR, later renamed Kering.

In the 2000s the G-Timeless became the brand's core collection, while the Gucci Dive, first a limited edition in 2013, became a permanent line in 2015. Under creative director Alessandro Michele, Gucci's watches embraced maximalist symbols such as bees, snakes and stars, and the unisex, skateboard-inspired Grip of 2019 became a cult hit. In 2021 Gucci launched its first High Watchmaking collection, anchored by the slim, integrated-bracelet 25H, followed by tourbillons and planetarium complications for the house's 50th anniversary of watchmaking in 2022. Watches are designed in Neuchâtel and assembled at Kering's manufacture in La Chaux-de-Fonds, with dials made at Fabbrica Quadranti in Ticino.

name: GUESS
tagline: Los Angeles glamour in glitzy, bold fashion watches since 1983
summary: GUESS is the Los Angeles denim and lifestyle brand founded by the Marciano brothers in 1981. Its watches, introduced in 1983 and today designed, made and distributed by Timex Group, are known for bold, crystal-embellished and gold-tone designs such as the barrel-shaped Venix, with the pricier Gc line above them.
history:
GUESS was founded in Los Angeles in 1981 by brothers Georges, Maurice, Armand and Paul Marciano, who had emigrated from Morocco via France. Its first hit was a stonewashed, slim-fit denim with ankle zippers, and the brand's black-and-white advertising campaigns, which launched the careers of models such as Claudia Schiffer and Anna Nicole Smith, made GUESS a defining name in 1980s and 1990s fashion.

Watches were among the first licensed categories. GUESS watches were introduced in 1983, bringing the brand's sexy, glamorous aesthetic to the wrist with crystal-set bezels, gold-tone bracelets and bold, oversized cases. The watch business is managed by Timex Group, which designs, manufactures and distributes GUESS watches worldwide alongside its other fashion licences such as Versace and Ferragamo. A more premium, largely Swiss-made sister line, Gc (Guess Collection), sits above the core range.

GUESS itself went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 1996 and grew into a global retailer with around 1,600 stores and roughly US$3 billion in annual revenue. In 2025 Authentic Brands Group, together with Maurice and Paul Marciano and partner Alberini, agreed a take-private deal in which Authentic acquired a majority of the GUESS intellectual property; the company delisted in January 2026. The watches continue under Timex Group, with collections such as Modern Icons for women and the barrel-cased Venix for men, alongside a growing number of automatic models.

name: Skagen
tagline: Ultra-thin Danish minimalism on a steel mesh bracelet
summary: Skagen is a Danish-inspired minimalist watch brand founded in 1989 by Henrik and Charlotte Jorst and named after Denmark's northernmost town. Famous for slim cases, clean stick-marker dials and Milanese mesh bracelets, it has been owned by Fossil Group since 2012.
history:
Skagen was founded in 1989 by Henrik and Charlotte Jorst, a Danish couple who had moved to the United States in 1986. Frustrated by the lack of simple, elegant watches in the US market, they began importing and designing slim, understated timepieces inspired by Scandinavian design. The brand was named after Skagen, Denmark's northernmost town, and its logo symbolises the meeting of the Skagerrak and Kattegat seas off its coast.

The Jorsts first showed their designs at a New York corporate gift fair in 1991 and began selling under their own brand in 1992, with about US$800,000 in first-year sales. Department stores including Bloomingdale's picked up the line in the mid-1990s, and ultra-thin steel watches on fine Milanese mesh bracelets became Skagen's signature. Sales approached US$30 million by 1998 and around US$70 million by 2005, as Skagen opened offices in Denmark and Hong Kong and expanded into jewellery. In 2010 its model 233 steel watch and Swiss Movement 585 series won Red Dot design awards.

In 2012 Fossil Group acquired Skagen Designs for roughly US$237 million, bringing it alongside Fossil's own brand as a house-owned label rather than a licence. Under Fossil, Skagen extended into hybrid and touchscreen smartwatches with the Falster and Jorn lines, while core analogue collections such as Signatur, Grenen, Ancher and Holst continued the brand's clean, Danish-inspired look. Skagen remains part of Fossil Group, which restructured its debt in 2025, and continues to use the Nordic coastline as its design muse.

name: Unimatic
tagline: Milanese 'design by removal' tool watches in black and matte steel
summary: Unimatic is a Milan-based microbrand founded in 2015 by industrial designers Giovanni Moro and Simone Nunziato. Its brutally minimal, 300m-rated tool watches, typically black-dialled with sandblasted or brushed steel and numbered casebacks, made it a cult favourite and a frequent collaborator with Hodinkee, Massena Lab and fashion houses.
history:
Unimatic was founded in Milan in 2015 by Giovanni Moro and Simone Nunziato, two industrial designers who wanted to apply a philosophy of 'design by removal' to the tool watch: every element had to serve a function, and anything decorative was stripped away. Their first watch, the Modello Uno, was a limited edition diver of 300 pieces with a stark black dial, pale-green lume and a matte steel case, inspired by mid-century Italian military and professional diving watches.

The brand quickly found an audience among collectors and fashion insiders alike. In 2016 Unimatic collaborated with the Paris concept store Colette and introduced the Modello Due, a 38mm time-only field-diver. The Modello Tre chrono-diver followed in 2018, and a steady run of limited editions and co-branded projects, including with Hodinkee and Massena Lab, turned new Unimatic releases into fast sell-outs. Nearly every model shares the same DNA: 300m water resistance, double-domed sapphire, a numbered screw-down caseback engraved with a 'Rosa dei Venti' compass rose, and Japanese Seiko-made movements.

In 2021 Unimatic set up its own assembly line near Milan, bringing assembly, testing and quality control in-house, and launched a permanent Classic line of individually numbered watches alongside the more technical Toolwatch series with GMT variants. In 2023 it partnered with Massena Lab on the 36mm Modello Cinque. Today Unimatic remains independent, designing and assembling its watches in Italy while continuing to release small, tightly edited limited editions.

name: anOrdain
tagline: Glasgow's enamel-dial workshop reviving high craft in British watchmaking
summary: anOrdain is a Glasgow watchmaker founded in 2016 by Lewis Heath, celebrated for vitreous enamel dials made entirely in its own Scottish workshop, including the world's first fumé enamel dials. With long waiting lists and a team of about 30 craftspeople, it has become one of the most admired British microbrands.
history:
anOrdain was incorporated in Glasgow in 2016 by Lewis Heath, a designer who had previously co-founded the Scottish headphone company RHA, working with a small founding team. The brand's name and philosophy centre on the idea that the best results come when designing and making happen under the same roof. Rather than outsourcing dials to Swiss suppliers, anOrdain set out to master vitreous enamel, one of the most difficult decorative crafts in watchmaking and traditionally the preserve of ultra-luxury maisons.

The first Model 1 watches paired Swiss movements with vividly coloured grand-feu style enamel dials and bespoke numerals inspired by the typography of old Scottish Highland maps. In 2019 anOrdain introduced what it describes as the world's first fumé enamel dials, in which colour graduates from a bright centre to a darker edge, and the Model 1 fumé became the brand's signature. The Model 2, a more compact and sporty design, followed, as did the Model 3 'Method' with a textured, hand-stamped enamel-on-silver dial and a porcelain-dial Model 1 that took three years to develop.

Demand quickly outstripped capacity, and anOrdain moved to a reservation-and-waiting-list system with lead times of many months. The team grew from three founders to around 30 people, including six specialist enamellers, and brought hand engraving, champlevé, porcelain, thermal bluing of hands, dial printing, type design, cold forging and leatherwork in-house. In 2025 the company moved into a purpose-designed factory on Glasgow's southside to expand production and train new craftspeople. anOrdain is a member of the Heritage Crafts Association and remains independent.

name: Studio Underd0g
tagline: Watermelons, pizza and mechanical chronographs: British watchmaking with a sense of humour
summary: Studio Underd0g is a British microbrand founded by designer Richard Benc in 2020 and launched on Kickstarter in 2021. Famous for playful fruit- and dessert-themed dials on affordable mechanical chronographs, it has grown into one of the most recognisable independent brands, collaborating with H. Moser & Cie. and opening its own assembly facility, the D0ghouse.
history:
Designer Richard Benc developed Studio Underd0g during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown, aiming to 'inject a bit of silliness' into an industry he saw as overly serious. The brand launched on Kickstarter in March 2021 with the 01Series, a 38.5mm manual-wind chronograph using the Seagull ST19 movement with 1940s-style pushers and dials in playful colourways such as Watermel0n, Desert Sky and Go0fy Panda, priced from about £325. The campaign reached its target within an hour.

The brand's zero-for-O naming, food-inspired dials and cheeky marketing built a devoted following. The 02Series of October 2023, a 37.5mm time-only watch with Studio Underd0g's first Swiss movement and a signature multi-layer sapphire dial, generated more than £1.8 million in sales in a nine-hour window. Collaborations followed with Time+Tide on pizza-themed watches, with Christopher Ward and Massena LAB, and, most surprisingly, with H. Moser & Cie. in 2024, pairing a Moser perpetual calendar with the first Underd0g monopusher chronograph in a US$64,900 'Passion Fruit' set. The monopusher 03Series became the brand's premium line, and a 2024 exclusive deal with Seagull underpinned a third-generation 01Series.

In December 2025 Studio Underd0g acquired its long-time British assembly workshop, renaming it Underd0g Manufacture and lifting capacity to more than 14,000 watches a year. In May 2026 it opened the D0ghouse in Maidenhead, a working facility where visitors can assemble their own watch, marking a shift from a virtual start-up to a British manufacturer with its own watchmakers.

name: Farer
tagline: British design, Swiss-made movements and a riot of colour
summary: Farer is an independent British watch company launched in 2015 and based in Berkshire, combining bold colours, textured dials and vintage-inspired cases with Swiss-made movements. Its direct-to-consumer range spans GMTs, compressor-style divers, racing chronographs, pilots and dress three-handers.
history:
Farer was incorporated in November 2014 by Paul Sweetenham, a designer and watch enthusiast, and launched its first collection in 2015. The founding idea was to revive the spirit of the 'halcyon era' of mid-century watchmaking, when bold colours and contrasting textures met serious craftsmanship, but to deliver it through a modern, direct-to-consumer model with no discounting. The brand's name evokes wayfaring and exploration, and many of its watches are named after explorers, ships and expeditions.

From the start Farer paired British design with Swiss manufacturing, working with Swiss partners on prototyping and production and fitting movements from Sellita and La Joux-Perret. Its signature became unexpected colour combinations: sea-green sunray dials with pillar-box red GMT hands, burnt-orange seconds hands, bronze crown caps and multi-level dials. The range grew to more than 40 models across a dozen collections, including the Lander GMT, the titanium Aqua Compressor divers with internal rotating bezels, hand-wound racing chronographs, pilot watches, world timers and a 35mm cushion-case line.

Farer has remained independent and founder-led, operating from an appointment-only showroom in the Berkshire countryside between Ascot and Bracknell. It offers a five-year movement guarantee, free worldwide shipping and complimentary engraving, and has become one of the best-known names in the wave of British independent brands that emerged in the 2010s.

name: Serica
tagline: Parisian instrument watches with enamel dials and COSC chronometer movements
summary: Serica is a Paris-based independent brand founded in 2019 by Jérôme Burgert and Gabriel Vachette. It makes compact, Swiss-made, COSC-certified 'instrument' watches, including field, dive and GMT chronometers and the Parade dress watch, known for enamel-look dials, lyre lugs and superb mesh bracelets.
history:
Serica was founded in Paris in 2019 by Jérôme Burgert and Gabriel Vachette with the aim of creating mechanical watches that combine robustness and technical sophistication with a singular, refined aesthetic. Rather than chasing trends, the founders conceived each collection as a precise instrument for a specific use, drawing on mid-century military, diving and aviation references while applying a distinctly French sense of proportion and finish.

The brand's early field and dive watches established its look: compact cases of 38-39mm, alternating polished and satin surfaces, lyre-shaped lugs, glossy black enamel-style dials with domed luminous indices, and double-domed sapphire crystals. Serica paid unusual attention to bracelets, offering woven 'Vesper' mesh, Bonklip-style and 'Expedition' bracelets with integrated end links. Its watches use Swiss-made Soprod movements, and in 2023 Serica achieved official COSC chronometer certification across its collections, an uncommon distinction at its price point.

The range now includes the Chronomètre Étanche field watches (refs. 6190 and 7505), the Chronomètre de Plongée divers (refs. 5303 and 5330) rated to 300m, the Chronomètre de Voyage GMT (ref. 8315) with a bi-colour ceramic bezel, and, since 2024, the Parade (ref. 1174), a slim stadium-shaped dress watch with a guilloché and sunburst dial. In 2025 Serica added new steel bracelets and limited editions. The company remains independent, selling direct and through its boutique on Rue de Turenne in Paris's Marais district.

name: Nezumi Studios
tagline: Stockholm-designed racing chronographs and tool watches, assembled in Germany
summary: Nezumi Studios is a Stockholm design studio founded in 2011 by David Campo that launched its first watch, the Voiture racing chronograph, in 2015. Its affordable, Scandinavian-clean chronographs, divers, GMTs and field watches are designed in Sweden and assembled in Germany.
history:
Nezumi Studios was founded in Stockholm in 2011 by David Campo, a designer and vintage sports-car and watch enthusiast who had spent nearly two decades in the fashion industry and wanted a place with total creative freedom. The studio's first project was not a watch at all but a limited run of 50 pairs of selvedge denim jeans made in Sweden, followed by leather goods and accessories. The name comes from Nezumi Kozō, a Japanese folk hero said to have stolen from rich samurai and given to the poor, reflecting the studio's support for charitable causes.

In 2015 Nezumi launched its first watch, the Voiture, a racing chronograph inspired by 1960s and 1970s motorsport, with a sandwich dial, three sub-registers and a tachymeter bezel. Powered by Seiko's VK mecha-quartz chronograph movement, it offered vintage racing style at an accessible price and quickly became the brand's signature. The Corbeau, a mil-spec-inspired chronograph with a 120-click bezel, and the Tonnerre, with a telemeter scale for measuring distance by the delay between lightning and thunder, extended the chronograph family.

Nezumi later broadened into automatic watches with the Baleine diver, the Aviera GMT with a Miyota 9075 true GMT movement and the Terrain field watch, alongside its own rubber, canvas and leather straps and Colin bracelets. The Voiture VM2 brought a slim automatic column-wheel chronograph to the line. Watches are designed and engineered in Stockholm and assembled, tested and quality-controlled in Germany, and Nezumi remains an independent, founder-led studio.

name: Autodromo
tagline: Vintage dashboard gauges and 1960s-80s racing cars, reimagined for the wrist
summary: Autodromo is a New York-based independent brand founded in 2011 by industrial designer and car enthusiast Bradley Price. Its watches translate the dashboards, gauges and design language of 1960s-1980s racing and road cars, from Group B rally to single-seat 'monoposto' racers, into compact, affordable timepieces.
history:
Bradley Price founded Autodromo in New York in 2011. A self-professed 'petrolhead' and owner of a Ferrari Dino 208 GT4, Price set out to capture the expression and passion of automobiles and timekeeping from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s. Rather than borrowing generic racing cues, Autodromo's designs draw directly on vintage dashboard instruments, speedometers and rev counters, while cases echo the wedge-era styling of Italian design studios such as Bertone.

The brand grew slowly and deliberately, releasing only a few watches each year. Early collections included the Monoposto, whose 43mm case recalls the oversized gauges of 1950s single-seater racing cars, and the Prototipo chronograph. The Group B, named after the famously wild 1980s rally category, became its best-known model, pairing a titanium bezel with a steel case and automatic Miyota movement. The Intereuropa, a hand-wound time-only watch on a Saffiano leather rally strap, and a Monoposto chronograph with a rev-counter-style redline followed, alongside collaborations such as a 2025 Group B 'Pegasus' edition with Mobil 1.

Autodromo has remained a small, independent and design-led company. In 2025 it re-issued the Monoposto as the limited Series Two with new colourways and a Miyota 9039 automatic, and in 2026 it launched the Group C Turbo Sport, a premium digital watch inspired by 1980s and 1990s Group C endurance racers. Beyond watches, Autodromo sells driving gloves, leather goods and apparel, rounding out a lifestyle brand for 'rev-heads who drive tastefully'.

name: Venezianico
tagline: Venetian art and architecture translated into accessible mechanical watches
summary: Venezianico is an Italian independent brand founded in late 2017 by brothers Alberto and Alessandro Morelli, based near Venice in San Donà di Piave. Its collections, named after Venetian landmarks, blend value-driven automatic watches with ambitious craft pieces, and in 2025 it unveiled the V5000, its first proprietary Italian-made movement.
history:
Brothers Alberto and Alessandro Morelli founded Venezianico in late 2017 while studying at Venice's Ca' Foscari University, combining a passion for watchmaking and design with their deep attachment to the city. The brand's logo was inspired by a detail they noticed while walking through St Mark's Square: the golden Renaissance cross atop the ancient Clock Tower, a symbol of the passage of time in Venice. Each collection takes its name and cues from Venetian history, architecture and the lagoon.

The Redentore, named after Andrea Palladio's Basilica del Redentore, is the brand's elegant everyday line in 36mm and 40mm, while the Nereide, named after the sea nymphs of myth, is a sporty 200m diver with a sunray dial, crystal-insert bezel and integrated 'Canova' bracelet. The Arsenale, named after the historic Venetian shipyards, is an integrated-bracelet sports watch with knurled bezel and exotic dials such as mother-of-pearl and meteorite, and the Bucintoro evokes the ceremonial galley of the Doges. Venezianico built a large following by offering Japanese automatic movements, sapphire crystals and striking dials at approachable prices, alongside a steady stream of limited editions and collaborations with retailers across Asia.

In 2025 Venezianico introduced the V5000, its first proprietary mechanical calibre, designed with and manufactured in Italy by OISA, a hand-wound 3.5Hz movement with 60 hours of power reserve. It debuted in the limited Redentore Utopia and powers the Grade 5 titanium Redentore Levius, whose Zefiro guilloché dial is hand-engraved on an 1850 rose engine. The company is headquartered in the Palazzo Baradel atelier in San Donà di Piave and aims to become Italy's reference name in watchmaking.

name: Dan Henry
tagline: A 1,500-watch collector's vintage icons, reissued at bargain prices
summary: Dan Henry is a direct-to-consumer brand created by Brazilian vintage collector Dan Henry, who amassed more than 1,500 watches over 30 years. Each model is named after a year and pays homage to a classic mid-century archetype, from racing chronographs to super-compressor divers, typically priced around US$300 and produced in numbered limited editions.
history:
Dan Henry's fascination with mechanical watches began when he received a Roskopf pocket watch for his tenth birthday. Over some 30 years of combing flea markets and local auctions he built a collection of more than 1,500 vintage watches, which he began sharing on Instagram and documented in Timeline.Watch, an online encyclopaedia of watch history. Many followers wanted watches like the ones he showed but could not afford or find the originals, and around 2016 he launched Dan Henry Watches to make comparable vintage-inspired designs accessible.

The brand's concept is simple: each watch is named after a year and distils the best elements of the era's classics. The 1970 Automatic Diver revisits the super-compressor divers of the late 1960s with twin crowns and an inner rotating bezel; the 1964 Gran Turismo recalls motorsport chronographs worn in the hills of California and the streets of Monaco; the 1962 Racing Chronograph channels racing drivers' watches of the Le Mans era; the 1963 is a pilot's GMT; and the 1975 is a slim skin diver. Other models reference 1937 dress chronographs, 1939 military chronographs and 1945 WWII chronographs. Most are issued as limited editions numbered to the model's year, such as 1,964 pieces for the 1964.

Dan Henry keeps prices low, mostly between US$250 and US$400, by selling direct with sapphire or sapphire-coated crystals and Japanese Seiko movements, including meca-quartz VK63 chronographs and NH35 and NH34 automatics. The brand ships from local warehouses in the US, EU and Brazil, and has become one of the most recommended entry points for collectors who love vintage design.

name: Spinnaker
tagline: Affordable automatic divers named after the pioneers of underwater exploration
summary: Spinnaker is an affordable dive-watch brand whose collections, such as Fleuss, Bradner, Piccard and Spence, are named after pioneers of diving and ocean exploration. It offers Japanese automatic divers with sapphire crystals at a few hundred dollars and is known for a steady stream of colourful limited editions and pop-culture collaborations.
history:
Spinnaker positions itself as a tribute to 'a life beneath, beyond and beside the sea', drawing on the golden age of diving and the daring spirit of early underwater pioneers. Each core collection is named after a figure from diving history: the Fleuss honours Henry Fleuss, whose 19th-century closed-circuit rebreather was a milestone in underwater breathing apparatus; the Bradner references Hugh Bradner, the physicist credited with inventing the modern wetsuit; and the Piccard nods to the Piccard family of deep-sea and stratospheric explorers. Other lines include the Spence, Hull, Croft, Cahill, Dumas, Challenger and Tesei.

The brand's formula is to put vintage-inspired dive-watch design, 316L steel cases, sapphire crystals, Swiss Super-LumiNova and Japanese Miyota or Seiko automatic movements into watches typically priced between about US$300 and US$600. Signature pieces include the Bradner, with its vintage proportions and bi-directional bezel; the Fleuss, a cushion-cased diver later reworked in a slimmer 40mm size; and the Spence 300, engineered to be only 11.5mm thick while offering 300m of water resistance.

Spinnaker is part of the Dartmouth Brands portfolio of affordable watch brands. In recent years it has become known for frequent limited editions and licensed collaborations with properties such as SpongeBob SquarePants, Popeye and Peanuts' Snoopy, as well as ocean-conservation partnerships with organisations including 4ocean and the Dolphin Project. It sells direct online worldwide and through retailers, with a two-year international warranty.

name: Pagani Design
tagline: Guangzhou's sapphire-crystal homage watches at bargain prices
summary: Pagani Design is a Chinese watch brand founded in Guangzhou in 2012 by Guangzhou Pagani Design Watch Co., Ltd. It is best known for inexpensive homage-style watches, echoing famous Swiss designs, with 316L steel cases, sapphire crystals and Japanese or Chinese movements, sold worldwide largely online.
history:
Pagani Design was established in Guangzhou, southern China, in 2012. Guangzhou and the surrounding Pearl River Delta are the heart of China's watch-making supply chain, and the brand grew out of that ecosystem with a straightforward proposition: make the look and specification of higher-end watches accessible to everyone. Its stated philosophy is that true horology should be defined by excellence rather than exclusivity.

The brand became widely known through online marketplaces such as AliExpress and Amazon, where its models, designated by 'PD' reference numbers, gained a following among budget-conscious enthusiasts. Many Pagani Design watches are openly inspired by iconic Swiss designs, including racing chronographs with tachymeter bezels, GMT travellers, fluted-bezel dress-sports watches and dive watches, while offering specifications unusual at their price, such as sapphire crystals, screw-down crowns, ceramic bezels and 100-200m water resistance. Movements include Seiko VK63 meca-quartz and Miyota quartz chronographs, Miyota 8215 automatics and Chinese Pearl GMT calibres.

In recent years the company has worked to strengthen its brand, launching an official global web store with a three-year warranty to distinguish genuine products from grey-market sellers, operating warehouses in the US, UK and Europe, and adding more ambitious pieces such as affordable mechanical tourbillons in its YS series. Pagani Design also operates the sister brand Benyar. It now sells across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Africa, and is one of the best-known names in the Chinese affordable-watch segment.

name: echo/neutra
tagline: Dolomites-inspired, Swiss-made watches from an Italian architect and aerospace engineer
summary: echo/neutra is an independent Italian brand created by architect-designer Nicola Callegaro and aerospace engineer Cristiano Quaglia. Its Swiss Made watches, powered by Sellita and ETA movements, range from the Dolomites-inspired Averau field watches and 500m Cristallo diver to 1950s-style 1956 chronographs and the ultra-thin titanium Rivanera, with a studio in Milan.
history:
echo/neutra was founded by two northern Italians with very different backgrounds. Nicola Callegaro is an architect and brand strategist who founded the design practice Zeppelin Studio in 2008 and has worked in object design for almost 20 years; Cristiano Quaglia is an aerospace engineer with a master's degree in propulsion systems and a passion for mountaineering in the Dolomites. Together they set out to create objects with 'a soul', balancing function and form, and to make watches that are 'not replicated, not repeated' and always unconventional.

The mountains became the brand's first muse. Its Averau collection, named after a Dolomite peak, is a contemporary field watch whose best-known version carries a 'Big Moon' moon phase in which a large convex moon rotates on itself, indicating the lunar phase both graphically and in text. The Cristallo, also named after a Dolomite massif, is a Swiss Made professional diver rated to 500m with a helium valve, ceramic no-decompression bezel, small seconds and power-reserve display from a Sellita SW279 movement.

echo/neutra then broadened its range with the 1956 collection, vintage-inspired chronographs and GMTs drawing on the 1950s and 1960s, including a hand-wound Sellita SW510 chronograph with ceramic telemeter bezel, and the Rivanera, an Art Deco-influenced dress-sports watch in Grade 5 titanium only 5.5mm thick and weighing 21 grams, powered by an ETA 7001. The company, ENCQ Srl, later opened Studio Milano, its first dedicated boutique space, in central Milan, and continues to release colourways and one-of-a-kind pieces in small numbers.

name: Bausele
tagline: Australian watches with a piece of Australia sealed inside the crown
summary: Bausele is a Sydney-based watch brand founded in 2011 by Swiss-born watchmaker Christophe Hoppé. Its name means 'Beyond Australian Elements', and its signature is a hollow crown holding real Australian materials such as Bondi or Manly Beach sand, red earth or opal, combined with Swiss movements.
history:
Bausele was founded in Sydney in 2011 by Christophe Hoppé, a Swiss-born watchmaker who had worked in the Swiss watch industry in Geneva and La Chaux-de-Fonds before moving to Australia. The name is derived from 'Beyond Australian Elements', and from the start Hoppé combined Australian design with Swiss movements and components. The brand's signature became a hollow crown containing small quantities of Australian materials, from Bondi Beach sand and outback red earth to coral, opal and sea glass.

The OceanMoon was one of Bausele's three founding watches in 2011; with a tide indicator, sea glass in the crown and a distinctive case it became the brand's most popular model and a favourite of surfers and ocean lovers. In 2015 Bausele became the first Australian watch brand to exhibit at Baselworld in Switzerland. The following year it formed a joint venture with Flinders University to develop 'Bauselite', a ceramic composite, used in the Terra Australis collection. Bausele also produced a Pilot Automatic with Australian aviation and military communities and collaborated with the Sydney Opera House and the Bathurst 12 Hour endurance race.

Military partnerships have become central to the brand. In 2021 Bausele made the official centenary watch of the Royal Australian Air Force, later followed by the Air Force 5th Generation, whose crown holds soil from RAAF Base Point Cook. In 2024 it launched the Elemental dive collection, developed with input from more than 400 contributors, and in 2026 released officially authorised 125th-anniversary watches for the Australian Army and the Royal Australian Engineers. Bausele remains privately held and headquartered in Sydney, and has shown at Geneva Watch Days.

name: Nicholas Hacko
tagline: Sydney's watchmaker who answered Swiss parts restrictions by building his own movements
summary: Nicholas Hacko is a Sydney master watchmaker, in business since 1981, who with his son Josh turned a repair workshop into Australia's only watch manufacture. After Swiss brands cut off spare parts, he launched the Rebelde brand, then in-house NH-series watches with movements designed and made in Australia, alongside the Soprod-powered Mark 1 and Mark II.
history:
Nicholas Hacko has worked as a master watchmaker, clockmaker and jeweller in Sydney since 1981, running a workshop in the Culwulla Chambers on Castlereagh Street that serviced prestige Swiss watches. Around 2011, as major Swiss brands began restricting the supply of spare parts to independent repairers, his livelihood came under threat. Rather than accept it, Hacko decided to make watches himself, beginning with a defiant '0/9' watch and, in 2013, the Rebelde brand, a 44mm California-dial watch in Pilot's and Control Tower styles, of which more than 700 were sold over six years.

In 2016 Nick and his son Josh, who had been sent to Switzerland for training, decided to build an in-house manufacturing facility in Sydney. They invested in a Citizen CNC lathe for bar-turning screws, pins and pinions, a Kern Pyramid Nano five-axis mill for plates, bridges and dials, an Affolter gear-hobbing machine and a Makino wire EDM. The result was the NH1, a 25-piece titanium watch with a manual-wind calibre manufactured in Australia and described as the first and only watch made there. The NH2 of 2019 became the first watch to use Timascus, a patterned layered-titanium material, in its movement, and the NH3 of 2021 added an in-house titanium guilloché dial and hands.

By 2020 the company could make up to 85 per cent of its watches in-house. Alongside the NH series it produces more accessible models: the Mark 1, a 40mm 1930s-style pilot's watch with a Swiss Soprod M100 movement assembled in Sydney, and the 2023 Mark II, whose anodised titanium dial is guilloché-engraved with waves inspired by Sydney's Curl Curl beach. Total output is around 50 to 100 watches a year.

name: Technos
tagline: A Swiss name that became Brazil's watch: Latin America's biggest watchmaker
summary: Technos began in 1900 as a Swiss watchmaker in Welschenrohr, Solothurn, but its brand rights passed to Brazil, where it is now the flagship of Grupo Technos, the largest watch company in Latin America. Assembled in Manaus, its watches, led by the iconic Skydiver diver, are among the most familiar in Brazil.
history:
Technos traces its roots to 1900, when Melchior Gunzinger founded a watch company in Welschenrohr in the Swiss canton of Solothurn. His son Joseph took over in 1920, renaming the business Gunzinger Bros Ltd and registering the Technos trademark in 1924. The company exported widely, and in the 1950s Technos watches arrived in Brazil, where an exclusive distributor, Importadora Centauro, founded in 1956, built the brand into a household name. Technos celebrates 1958 as the year of its arrival in Brazil.

In Switzerland the firm moved to Biel/Bienne in 1977 and changed hands several times during the quartz-crisis era, passing to General Watch Co. in 1970 and to the Japanese importer Heiwado in 1982. Meanwhile the Brazilian business opened an assembly plant in the Manaus free-trade zone in 1982. In the 1990s the Brazilian company acquired the Technos rights for South America, and in 2002 the remaining worldwide rights, making Technos a fully Brazilian brand. The Skydiver, a dive watch first introduced in the 1960s, became its icon, and the 1986 Skydiver Anadigi, combining analogue hands with a digital display, became a Brazilian classic.

Grupo Technos went public in 2011 and built a multi-brand portfolio including Mormaii, Euro, Condor, Mariner, Allora, Touch and Dumont, plus licensed and distributed brands such as Fossil and Michael Kors. It launched e-commerce and its own stores in the 2010s and connected watches from 2015. Today the group, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro with production in Manaus, describes itself as the largest watch company in Latin America, producing around a million watches a year, and in 2026 celebrated 40 years of the Skydiver Anadigi.

name: Caveman Watches
tagline: Made by Ghanaian artisans: Accra's award-winning homegrown watch brand
summary: Caveman Watches is an Accra-based Ghanaian watch company founded in December 2018 by Anthony Dzamefe, who began by selling watches in Kantamanto Market. It designs, hand-assembles and personalises watches and handmade straps in Ghana, and its Blue Volta was named Ghana's Product of the Year in 2021.
history:
Anthony Mensah Dzamefe started out in 2015 selling second-hand and replica watches in Accra's Kantamanto Market, buying his first watch for GH₵50 and reselling it at a profit. He learned to make leather watch straps from a cobbler and began repairing broken watches, gradually building the skills and customer base that would let him create his own brand. On 12 December 2018 he launched Caveman Watches in Ghana, with the ambition of building a Ghanaian watch manufacturing company whose products are 'made by Ghanaian artisans, built to last generations'.

The brand's first and best-known watch, the Blue Volta, launched with the company in 2018. It pairs a blue Pantone sun-ray dial with luminous hands and a date window in a slim 6mm stainless-steel case, offered in 42mm and 36mm sizes on leather straps or chain bracelets. It became a fan favourite among corporate professionals, and in 2021 won Product of the Year at the Ghana Manufacturing Awards, where Caveman was also named watch manufacturing company of the year; the brand was also named Brand of the Year at the EMY Africa Awards.

Caveman has since expanded into collections such as Classics, Heritage, Aviator and higher-end automatic pieces such as the Liege, along with wall clocks, jewellery and accessories. A signature of the brand is personalisation, with engraved dials and case sides, and bespoke commissions for public figures, including a customised watch for Ghanaian footballer Asamoah Gyan. Profiled by The New York Times and Forbes, Caveman is one of Africa's most visible homegrown watch brands and runs its operations from Accra.

name: CLUSE
tagline: Amsterdam's affordable-luxury minimalist watches with swappable straps
summary: CLUSE is an Amsterdam fashion-accessories brand founded in 2013, best known for minimalist women's watches with interchangeable straps at around €100. Designed in-house in Amsterdam and sold online and through retailers worldwide, it has since expanded into jewellery, bags and men's watches.
history:
CLUSE was founded in Amsterdam in 2013. Its founders saw a gap in the market: luxury watches offered beautiful design at high prices, while affordable watches too often lacked style and craftsmanship. CLUSE set out to create 'affordable luxury' watches combining timeless design and functionality sold at accessible prices.

The brand's early success rested on clean, feminine designs: slim round and square cases in silver, gold and rose-gold tones, minimalist dials, mesh bracelets and leather straps that customers could change themselves using quick-release fittings in standard CLUSE widths. Collections such as Minuit, Triomphe, La Tétragone, Gracieuse, Féroce and Boho Chic became staples, and CLUSE built a network of retailers and stockists alongside its own webshop, with collections designed by an in-house team in Amsterdam through a process of moodboards, sketching, material selection and detail refinement.

Over time CLUSE broadened from watches into jewellery and bags, positioning its accessories as 'an extension of your personality' that can be mixed and matched. It has also added more ambitious timepieces, including the integrated-bracelet Vigoureux line for men with chronograph and automatic versions, and multifunction models such as the Quadrus. The business is operated by Europe Watch Group B.V. from Amsterdam and remains one of the best-known Dutch watch brands.

name: Olivia Burton
tagline: Vintage-inspired London watches with bees, florals and British charm
summary: Olivia Burton is a London fashion watch and jewellery brand launched in 2012, known for vintage-inspired women's watches with signature bee motifs, floral dials and mesh bracelets. One of the UK's fastest-growing fashion watch brands, it has been owned by Movado Group since 2017.
history:
Olivia Burton was founded in London and launched in 2012 by Jemma Finch and Lesa Bennett, who set out to create vintage-inspired, design-led watches for women at accessible prices. Drawing on vintage finds, contemporary fashion and a strong sense of British style, the brand quickly became known for small-to-mid-sized dials, floral prints, mesh bracelets and playful details, sold through UK department stores and its own webshop.

Its signature motif became the bee, used on dials, crowns and later jewellery, alongside Mini Dial watches, bee-motif dials and the honeycomb pattern. Collections are often named after London places, such as the Grosvenor, inspired by the clean lines and geometry of London's streets and squares, as well as Westbourne, Highbury and Pembroke. The brand's growth was rapid, and it was widely described as one of the United Kingdom's fastest-growing fashion watch and jewellery brands.

In July 2017 US-based Movado Group, owner of Movado, Concord and Ebel and licensee of brands such as Tommy Hilfiger and Hugo Boss, completed its acquisition of Olivia Burton. Under Movado, the brand expanded internationally and grew its jewellery business, with motifs such as the honeycomb and North Star. Today Olivia Burton's range spans tiny 16mm Mini Grove watches to 30mm Classic Bee and Westbourne designs, mostly with quartz movements and gold, rose-gold, silver and two-tone ion-plated steel cases, with watches designed to be gifted, stacked with bracelets and worn every day.

name: Tommy Hilfiger
tagline: Classic American cool in red, white and blue, on the wrist since 2001
summary: Tommy Hilfiger is the preppy American lifestyle brand founded in 1985 and owned by PVH Corp. since 2010. Its watches, launched in 2001 and designed, made and distributed under licence by Movado Group, are affordable quartz and automatic pieces with sporty, nautical and racing styling and the brand's red-white-and-blue accents.
history:
Designer Tommy Hilfiger launched his eponymous label in New York in 1985 with backing from Indian textile magnate Mohan Murjani, famously announcing himself with a Times Square billboard that placed his name alongside America's great designers. The brand's preppy, all-American style, flag logo and red, white and blue palette made it one of the defining fashion labels of the late 1980s and 1990s, embraced by hip-hop artists as well as the country-club set.

Tommy Hilfiger expanded rapidly into accessories through licensing. In 2001 Movado Group launched Tommy Hilfiger watches under an exclusive licence, and the line became one of Movado's most important licensed businesses, selling through department stores, Tommy Hilfiger stores and online worldwide. The watches are typically quartz multifunction and chronograph designs in steel, ion-plated or silicone-strapped cases, often with navy dials, red accents and nautical or motorsport details, plus a women's range of mesh-bracelet and crystal-set pieces.

The company itself changed hands several times: it was taken private by Apax Partners in 2006 and bought by PVH Corp., owner of Calvin Klein, for about US$3 billion in 2010, with its global headquarters now in Amsterdam. Movado's Tommy Hilfiger watch licence has been repeatedly extended and currently runs through 31 December 2029. Recent additions include vintage racing-inspired chronographs and the TH85, a 40mm Japanese automatic with a coin-edge rotating bezel, 100m water resistance and exhibition caseback, signalling a push toward more serious watch specifications.
